persona.name: Elodie Vasseur

occupation.title: Regulatory Affairs Manager
occupation.organization: A mid-size pharmaceutical company headquartered in the 15th arrondissement of Paris
occupation.description: Shepherds drug dossiers through European approval procedures — deadline-driven document work, calls with notified bodies, and a steady drip of compliance emails. Leaves the office around 19h most days, later during submission crunches. Commutes 40 minutes each way on line 12.

persona.education: PharmD from Universite Paris-Saclay followed by a specialized master's in regulatory affairs; did an Erasmus year in Bologna she still talks about.
long_term_goals: Move to a two-bedroom apartment with a real kitchen, ideally near Parc Montsouris
Stop eating dinner at 21h30 out of exhaustion
Take a full month off to walk part of the Camino de Santiago with her partner
persona.style: Organized and measured — she answers questions the way she writes regulatory summaries, with caveats and numbered reasons. Warm once the practical questions are settled, but she always asks about the fine print first. Dresses in quiet, well-cut basics and keeps a running list app for everything, including grievances. Will absolutely read the cancellation policy before the product description.

traits: Cautiously optimistic about services that save time
Tired in a way she jokes about

interests: Batch cooking on Sunday afternoons (aspirational, rarely happens)
likes: Her partner doing the dishes unprompted
Lists that get fully checked off
Season 3 of anything she already trusts
dislikes: Subscriptions that hide the cancel button
Wasting half a bunch of coriander
Recipes that claim 20 minutes and take 50

beliefs: Time after work belongs to us, not to logistics
A good system beats good intentions
You vote with your wallet, so read what you sign
Eating well on weeknights shouldn't require heroics
skills: Reading contractual fine print at speed
Weeknight improvisation with whatever Picard has

general: Does one big Leclerc drive order per week, then forgets one key ingredient
Screenshots promo codes and forgets to use them
Compares any new service against 'what Picard already gives me'
Cancels free trials on day 27 with calendar reminders

morning: 6h45 alarm, espresso from the machine, out by 7h30
Podcast on the metro — usually news or a nutrition one she half-trusts
workday: Lunch at the company RIE or a salad from the Franprix downstairs
evening: Home by 19h45, dinner decision negotiation with Marc
One episode of a series, in bed by 23h15
weekend: Saturday market at Rue Daguerre when motivated
Sunday: yoga, meal-prep attempt, calls to her mother in Tours

health.physical: Generally fine; recurring lower-back stiffness from desk work, sees an osteopath twice a year.
health.mental: Steady but running near capacity; guards her Sundays fiercely.

relationships.name: Marc Vasseur
relationships.description: A financial controller with worse hours than hers; sweet, useless at meal planning, excellent at reheating.

relationships.name: Camille
relationships.description: Lives in Lyon, subscribed to a meal kit last year and won't stop recommending it — Elodie is 60% convinced, 40% suspicious.

relationships.name: Francoise Vasseur
relationships.description: Retired schoolteacher in Tours who thinks buying pre-portioned ingredients is 'giving up'; they argue about it fondly.
